title: Build a Django CRUD App with Admin Panel
description: Create a Django project with models, migrations, admin customization, and template-based views for student management
objective: Students will create a Django project from scratch, define models with relationships, customize the admin panel, and build views with templates to list, create, and search students

steps.title: Create the Django Project and App
steps.instructions:
Open your terminal and run these commands to set up a new Django project:

```bash
pip install django
django-admin startproject institute
cd institute
python manage.py startapp students
```

Now add the app to `institute/settings.py`:

```python
INSTALLED_APPS = [
    'django.contrib.admin',
    'django.contrib.auth',
    'django.contrib.contenttypes',
    'django.contrib.sessions',
    'django.contrib.messages',
    'django.contrib.staticfiles',
    'students',   # <-- add this line
]
```

Run the initial migration and start the server:

```bash
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py runserver
```

Open http://localhost:8000 in your browser. You should see the Django welcome page with a rocket.

Create a superuser for the admin panel:

```bash
python manage.py createsuperuser
# Username: admin
# Email: admin@techpath.biz
# Password: admin123 (for development only)
```

Visit http://localhost:8000/admin/ and log in with your superuser credentials.

steps.title: Define Models and Run Migrations
steps.instructions:
Open `students/models.py` and define two models:

```python
from django.db import models
from django.core.validators import MinValueValidator, MaxValueValidator


class Course(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100, unique=True)
    duration_months = models.IntegerField(default=6)
    fee = models.DecimalField(max_digits=8, decimal_places=2)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['name']


class Student(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    email = models.EmailField(unique=True)
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=15, blank=True)
    city = models.CharField(max_length=50, default='Bhopal')
    course = models.ForeignKey(Course, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='students')
    marks = models.IntegerField(
        default=0,
        validators=[MinValueValidator(0), MaxValueValidator(100)]
    )
    enrolled_on = models.DateField(auto_now_add=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.name} ({self.course.name})"

    class Meta:
        ordering = ['-enrolled_on']
```

Create and apply migrations:

```bash
python manage.py makemigrations
python manage.py migrate
```

You should see output like:
```
Migrations for 'students':
  students/migrations/0001_initial.py
    - Create model Course
    - Create model Student
```

Open the Django shell and add sample data:

```bash
python manage.py shell
```

```python

# Create courses

web_course = Course.objects.create(name='Web Development', duration_months=4, fee=25000)

Student.objects.create(name='Vikram Joshi', email='vikram@email.com', city='Pune', course=web_course, marks=45)
Student.objects.create(name='Neha Gupta', email='neha@email.com', city='Bhopal', course=python_course, marks=88)

print(f'Created {Student.objects.count()} students')
exit()
```

steps.title: Customize the Admin Panel
steps.instructions:
Open `students/admin.py` and register your models with customization:

```python
from django.contrib import admin
from .models import Student, Course


@admin.register(Course)
class CourseAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    list_display = ['name', 'duration_months', 'fee', 'is_active', 'student_count']
    list_filter = ['is_active']
    search_fields = ['name']

    def student_count(self, obj):
        return obj.students.count()
    student_count.short_description = 'Enrolled'


@admin.register(Student)
class StudentAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin):
    list_display = ['name', 'email', 'course', 'city', 'marks', 'enrolled_on']
    list_filter = ['course', 'city']
    search_fields = ['name', 'email']
    list_per_page = 20
    list_editable = ['marks']
    readonly_fields = ['enrolled_on']
    actions = ['mark_as_passed']

    @admin.action(description='Set marks to 40 for failing students')
    def mark_as_passed(self, request, queryset):
        updated = queryset.filter(marks__lt=40).update(marks=40)
        self.message_user(request, f'{updated} students updated.')
```

Visit http://localhost:8000/admin/ and explore:

1. Click on Students — you should see the list with all columns
2. Try the search box — search for "Rahul"
3. Use the filters on the right — filter by course or city
4. Edit marks directly in the list view (click, change, save)
5. Select students with checkboxes and use the "Mark as passed" action
6. Click on Courses — check the student count column

Take a screenshot of the admin panel showing student list.

steps.title: Create Views and Templates
steps.instructions:
Create a templates directory: ```bash mkdir -p students/templates/students ``` Create `students/templates/students/list.html`: ```html TechPath Institute — Students

TechPath Institute — Student List

{{ total }}

Total Students

{% for student in students %} {% empty %} {% endfor %}
# Name Email Course City Marks Status
{{ forloop.counter }} {{ student.name }} {{ student.email }} {{ student.course.name }} {{ student.city }} {{ student.marks }} {% if student.marks >= 40 %} Pass {% else %} Fail {% endif %}
No students found.
``` Create the view in `students/views.py`: ```python from django.shortcuts import render from django.db.models import Q from .models import Student, Course def student_list(request): students = Student.objects.select_related('course').all() search = request.GET.get('search', '') if search: students = students.filter( Q(name__icontains=search) | Q(email__icontains=search) ) course_id = request.GET.get('course') if course_id: students = students.filter(course_id=course_id) context = { 'students': students, 'courses': Course.objects.all(), 'search': search, 'total': students.count(), } return render(request, 'students/list.html', context) ``` Create `students/urls.py`: ```python from django.urls import path from . import views urlpatterns = [ path('', views.student_list, name='student-list'), ] ``` Update `institute/urls.py`: ```python from django.contrib import admin from django.urls import path, include urlpatterns = [ path('admin/', admin.site.urls), path('', include('students.urls')), ] ``` Visit http://localhost:8000/ to see your student list with search and filter.

steps.title: Practice ORM Queries in the Shell
steps.instructions:
Open the Django shell and practice these queries:

```bash
python manage.py shell
```

Run each query one by one and note the output:

```python
from students.models import Student, Course
from django.db.models import Q, Avg, Count, Max

# 1. Get all students
print('All students:', Student.objects.all())

# 2. Get students from Bhopal
print('Bhopal:', Student.objects.filter(city='Bhopal'))

# 3. Students with marks >= 80
print('Toppers:', Student.objects.filter(marks__gte=80))

# 4. Search by name (case-insensitive)
print('Search:', Student.objects.filter(name__icontains='rahul'))

# 5. OR query — Bhopal OR Delhi
print('B or D:', Student.objects.filter(Q(city='Bhopal') | Q(city='Delhi')))

# 6. Exclude failures
print('Passed:', Student.objects.exclude(marks__lt=40))

# 7. Aggregate — average marks
print('Average:', Student.objects.aggregate(avg=Avg('marks')))

# 8. Count students per course
result = Course.objects.annotate(count=Count('students'))
for c in result:
    print(f'{c.name}: {c.count} students')

# 9. Top scorer
top = Student.objects.order_by('-marks').first()
print(f'Topper: {top.name} with {top.marks} marks')

# 10. Update all Bhopal students marks +5
from django.db.models import F
Student.objects.filter(city='Bhopal').update(marks=F('marks') + 5)
print('Updated Bhopal marks')

# 11. select_related (avoid N+1)
for s in Student.objects.select_related('course'):
    print(f'{s.name} -> {s.course.name}')

exit()
```
